cards.headline: Common errors in maths exams and how to avoid them
bullets: Careless mistakes in maths exams are common but fixable, say educators.
Pupils may rush, misread questions, or have messy handwriting, leading to lost marks.
Not checking work properly or jumping to conclusions are also common errors.
Teachers suggest strategies like slowing down, checking work, and time management to avoid mistakes.

cards.headline: Passenger rescued after being trapped in lorry following accident in Woodlands
bullets: A lorry passenger was freed after being stuck in the vehicle following an accident in Woodlands.
The accident happened at the junction of Woodlands Avenue 6 and Woodlands Avenue 1.
SCDF used special tools to rescue the trapped passenger.
The rescued person was conscious and sent to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

cards.headline: Meet Toy Story 5 characters at VivoCity, Gardens by the Bay
bullets: Toy Story 5 characters are at VivoCity and Gardens by the Bay until June 28 and March 14, 2027.
VivoCity has a play area like Bonnie's room with character photo spots and carnival games.
Kids can ride pedal karts at VivoCity for free if they are among the first 500 new Kids Club members.
Gardens by the Bay features Toy Story topiaries, including Jessie, Woody, and Buzz Lightyear, in its floral exhibition.
The Gardens by the Bay exhibition also includes Winnie the Pooh and Singapore-themed Disney character displays.

cards.headline: Singapore’s revised driving licence requirements extended to all EVs up to 3,000kg from June 15
bullets: From June 15, drivers with Class 3 or 3A licences can drive electric vehicles up to 3,000kg.
This is an increase from the previous 2,500kg limit for electric light goods vehicles and small buses.
Existing licence holders automatically qualify for this change without needing updates.
This move supports Singapore's goal to use only clean-energy vehicles by 2040.

cards.headline: Phone Sleeps First: NTU student project helps undergrads put phones away for better sleep
bullets: NTU students ran a campaign to help university students sleep better by reducing phone use.
Over 300 students joined the "Phone Sleeps First" project to cut down late-night scrolling.
Participants reduced their phone time before bed by about an hour each night.
The project showed that less phone use led to more energy and better sleep habits.

cards.headline: I-dle Syncopation Singapore concert: K-pop queens show off immense charisma, powerful vocals and a JJ Lin cover
bullets: K-pop group I-dle performed in Singapore on Saturday, covering JJ Lin's song 'Whenever'.
The concert featured powerful vocals, impressive choreography, and a lot of pyrotechnics.
Fans enjoyed the distinct charms and energetic performances of each of the five members.
The show included hits, B-sides, and solo songs from the popular girl group.

cards.headline: How a restored Singapore shophouse became a home for art, Danish design and family memories
bullets: A restored Mount Sophia shophouse now blends old architecture with Danish design and art.
The home features preserved details like the pintu pagar and new extensions for family.
Owner Lena Koh's travels and art passion shaped the eclectic, harmonious interiors.
The house is featured in a new book showcasing adapted Singapore shophouses.

cards.headline: PSA pays fine over worker's death at Keppel Terminal in 2017, but appeals guilty verdict and sentence
bullets: PSA paid a S$225,000 fine after a worker died in 2017.
The company was found guilty of failing to ensure worker safety.
A worker was crushed to death while fixing a crane.
PSA is appealing against the guilty verdict and the fine.

cards.headline: Can’t get enough of CJ Hendry’s plush flowers? Here are 4 Singapore makers crafting blooms that last
bullets: Local makers craft lasting flowers from yarn, paper, and pipe cleaners.
Some local makers also offer workshops to teach you how to create your own flowers.
Prices for these handcrafted bouquets range from under S$80 to S$250.
Singer Nathan Hartono recently praised a local crochet flower maker online.
Paper flower artists have even created works for brands like Kenzo.

cards.headline: Puppies, ponies and Pilates: I tried some of Singapore’s most unconventional fitness classes
bullets: From yoga with rescued cats to Pilates alongside puppies, ponies and the world’s tallest indoor waterfall, these classes are turning exercise into an experience
See the article for full details.

cards.headline: Gold fever sends some vintage luxury watches to the melting furnace
bullets: Gold prices are so high that some luxury watches are being melted down.
The value of the gold in some older Omega and Tag Heuer watches is now more than what they sell for.
One dealer melted a 1970s Omega Constellation, getting 35% more for the gold than its auction price.
Some brand new, unsold watches are also being melted because too many were made.
High-end brands like Rolex are less likely to be melted because they hold their value better.

cards.headline: Rolex raises gold watch prices again as super-rich buyers are undeterred
bullets: Rolex raised gold watch prices by 5% globally this month.
This is the second price increase for Rolex gold watches this year.
Other luxury brands like Cartier also increased their gold watch prices.
Demand for expensive watches remains high among wealthy buyers.
Some rare Rolex models have seen prices jump over 30% since 2024.

cards.headline: Emaar to develop US$55b real estate project in Dubai: founder
bullets: Emaar plans a US$55 billion (S$74 billion) new city in Dubai.
The massive project will house 150,000 people in homes, offices, and shops.
It is Emaar's biggest project ever, aiming to boost Dubai's property market.
Dubai's property market saw record deals last year despite regional issues.

cards.headline: ‘Important to remain involved’: Why StanChart didn’t walk away from the Singapore Marathon
bullets: Standard Chartered is now the official bank partner for the Singapore Marathon, sponsoring the 10 km race.
The bank was the title sponsor for 24 years, helping the event grow significantly.
Standard Chartered also recently became a partner for Formula 1 races globally.
The bank sees its sports sponsorships as long-term commitments to clients, colleagues, and the community.

cards.headline: HK$563 million sale of mansion to Singapore citizen among Hong Kong’s largest property deals in 2026
bullets: A Singapore citizen bought a Hong Kong mansion for S$92.3 million.
This was one of the biggest property sales in Hong Kong in 2026.
The historic home is over 6,100 sq ft and located in Shek O.
The buyer is married to a China-born billionaire who is also a Singaporean.

cards.headline: Woman allegedly gets hand caught in blender at Tampines condo, sent to hospital
bullets: A woman's hand got stuck in a blender at a Tampines condo on June 10.
She was taken to Changi General Hospital.
Fire trucks, ambulances, and police were seen at the scene.
Her hand was reportedly not broken.

cards.headline: Driver of S'pore car gets into accident in Johor, says he won't run away, poses for camera, later drives off
bullets: A Singapore car driver crashed in Johor, promised not to flee, then drove off.
The driver appeared drunk and posed for photos before leaving the scene.
The other car involved sustained damage to its door and fender.
The incident was caught on video and shared online, sparking public anger.

cards.headline: Myanmar woman, 34, found dismembered & stuffed in plastic box in Bangkok apartment, husband wanted by police
bullets: A dismembered body of a 34-year-old Myanmar woman was found in a plastic box in a Bangkok apartment.
Police are searching for her missing body parts, including her head.
Her husband, also from Myanmar, is wanted for questioning over her suspected murder.
He was seen leaving the apartment with a large suitcase, according to CCTV footage.

cards.headline: The Former Teacher’s Training College In Orchard Was SG’s First Permanent Teacher-Training Institution
bullets: Singapore's first permanent teacher-training college opened in 1950.
The college trained teachers for primary schools in English, Malay, Chinese, and Tamil.
It moved to Paterson Road in 1955 to train more teachers for growing student numbers.
The campus later housed other schools and training facilities after teacher training moved.
The former college site is a quiet reminder of Singapore's education history in Orchard.

cards.headline: VivoCity Has A Toy Story Carnival This June Holiday With Games, Pedal Karts & Free Merch
bullets: VivoCity is holding a Toy Story carnival until June 28.
Enjoy carnival games, pedal karts, and train rides for $10 each.
Win Toy Story plushies or pins from claw machines for $2 a try.
Complete a stamp rally to get a free sticker set.
Spend $250 to get a free Toy Story lunch kit.

cards.headline: A Skater’s Guide To 12 Best Rollerblading Trails In Singapore, Ranked From Beginner To Expert
bullets: The Great Eastern Promenade is a sheltered, beginner-friendly rollerblading spot in Kallang.
East Coast Park offers flat paths from Parkland Green to Bedok Jetty, good for beginners.
Punggol coastal trail has smooth, wide paths, suitable for intermediate skaters.
Skating trails are ranked by slopes, path smoothness, safety from traffic, and ease of access.
